India Oṃ namaḥ śivāya | Salutations again and again to that Śiva, the bestower of auspiciousness.
Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self. Oṃ, salutation to the Remover of Obstacles. Now, the Essence of the Haṃsa is being written.
"O Lord, I have previously heard the stainless *Haṃsayāmala*;
now I desire to hear again that which is the supreme essence of essences. (1)
O God, that which was previously spoken by you has been merely indicated and not fully revealed;
tell me the true nature of that reality. O Wielder of the Trident, grant me your grace. (2)
Excellent, excellent, O one of great wisdom, who awakens for the sake of all sentient beings!
For that purpose, O Great Goddess, I shall speak out of affection for you. (3)
He who is that peaceful, unborn God, the support of power and devoid of form, is difficult to attain for all the gods as well as for the yoginīs.
Existing as the life-force, he always abides in the left, the right, and the middle;
and he is the supreme haṃsa, indeed that eternal God. (5)
He is Brahmā, he is indeed Rudra, and he is Īśvara and Viṣṇu as well;
he is Sadāśiva, the supreme abode, and the Tāraka Brahman itself.
O Goddess of gods, in Vārāṇasī one's own path has been revealed;
that sacred field is established as the state of non-knowledge for the wise who abide without vows.
I shall describe its characteristic, by which practitioners will recognize it;
for that is the transition to the state of the Guru, which is seen but not perceived.
That supreme Self is indeed situated everywhere in a state of mobility;
for it, abiding both within and without, vibrates within all embodied beings.
He is eternally risen and yet established; beginningless, he is the Lord of dissolution.
He is unmanifest and yet possesses manifest form; he is ungraspable, both moving and unmoving.

Grasped through meditative cultivation, consisting of pure consciousness, and established in the firmness of sentience—the Supreme Lord, whose form is light, indeed abides within the space of the heart. || 11 ||
Situated in the external sky, smoke-colored, with a body whose nature is the tip of smoke; pure like a crystal, it is yet distinct within the sky, like the sky itself. (12)
The creeper of liberation has that form, coiled with various twists;
it resembles a bee and consists of the letter *ha* without its head-stroke (*śira*).
The supreme, peaceful Lord of the Family is seen as the lineage;
he is truly a Siddha, for one beholds flowers within that very [vision]. 14.
The Supreme Lord is seen through the divisions of one and many, through millions of distinctions, and through the differentiation of various forms. || 15 ||
Appearing at night within the house, he is seen as tawny and blazing;
possessing the form of the light of the true sky, he roars again and again. (16)
O Goddess, for him who day by day offers the external and internal object of focus, there shall be no birth in any womb, nor shall there be even a portion of sin.
"O fair-faced one, he who has been devoted to Śiva-bhakti for thousands of previous births—his final birth is seen as that of a *haṃsa*. (18)
The knot of the heart is rent asunder, all doubts are cut away, and his karmas are exhausted when that which is both high and low is seen. 19.
Indeed, a teacher who bestows the knowledge of the Haṃsa is difficult to find; there is no object on earth that, by giving it, one might attain [liberation] through conduct. 20.
Now, therefore, O Ambika, I shall fully explain the knowledge of time and the thorough understanding of the signs of time for yogins, so that they do not fall into lower states of existence. (21)
O Goddess, that which has the crooked form of a serpent at the front of all the threads—even by seeing that for a long time, rebirth no longer exists. || 22 ||
Through the *ṛk* mantra, liberation occurs when the form is that of a *liṅga*; through the *ghanas*, bondage comes to be.
When the body is red, one should know [the result], and in yellow, there is the attainment of wealth. (23)
By the beasts of prey, there is a special movement; by the *bindu* and *nāda*, there is clarity.
There is abundance in the case of movement, and famine in the case of the "beak" (*cañcu*) being bound. (24)
If there is a break in the middle, one dies within three months; of this there is no doubt. When joined with three days [of breathlessness], one will certainly die thereafter. (25)
In the forenoon, O fair-faced one, having seen the [deity] established as before, the wise practitioner should perform the visualization with palms joined over a vessel filled with water. (26)
Standing at the junction of the Samā, having gone to the south, one should predict death after six months;
one should observe day and night through the division of the Moon and the Sun. || 27 ||
For two months [the sun moves] with the moon and the sun; for one month it is with the moon in the southern path.
In the east, on the new moon day of the southern course, it enters the solar disc.
On the new moon day for ten days, and for five days during the Sūryagottara [festival],
O beautiful one, this single cycle of time has been described to you.
"O Lord, how does one truly know the deception of time?
Pray, explain this doubt to me, for I have great curiosity regarding it. (30)
Listen, O Goddess of virtuous vows, to this supreme secret, a mystery difficult to find on earth; that which has not been told to anyone, I shall declare to you.
O Dear One, one should visualize the syllable *ṭha* in the center of the lunar disc; one should diligently contemplate the *haṃsa* situated within the middle of the *ṭha*. (32)
Flowing from the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) and consisting of the supreme nectar, she is imperishable, all-pervading, subtle, supreme, and the highest power of this [Lord]. (33)
O beloved, one should contemplate that river situated within the belly of the swan;
here, neither time nor old age or disease can prevail.
O Goddess, praised by heroes, the deception of time must be guarded;
O Mistress of practitioners, the Mothers desire the presence of one who is protected. (35)
Therefore, with every effort, this should not be given to just anyone;
it should be given to those endowed with devotion whose souls delight in devotion to the Guru. (36)
The Guru should be known as one who has gone to Śiva, and Śiva is that which has emerged from the mouth of the Guru;
he who is the Guru is Śiva himself in person, and he should be worshipped with diligent effort. (37)
Pure, skillful, and humble, his power is also fully realized;
for him, both knowledge and liberation are accomplished in the ultimate sense. (38)
When the mind is absorbed in that state, free from all mental fluctuations,
one will become liberated from wrinkles and grey hair within six months.
One should not calculate time here, nor is there any disease;
it is the essence of the *haṃsa*, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Void, and the Supreme Śiva. (40)
This collection of swans and cranes is renowned for the sake of your welfare;
it must not be given to atheists, nor to the deceitful, nor to those of cruel mind.
For those who are hypocritical, lacking devotion, and whose souls delight in the conduct of the Tantras are like beasts and insects, excluded from the Great Path.
Burnt by the conceptualization of doubt, afflicted by the blindness of great delusion, lacking confidence and finding no satisfaction, they are conditioned by the scriptures of the beasts.
They do not obtain that supreme, incomparable totality of the flood, which is agitated by a multitude of great waves and has come forth from the mouth of the Guru. (34)
Therefore, O Goddess worshipped by heroes, it should be given with every effort to one who is devoted to the guru, who is peaceful, and who delights in constant practice.
To the one seated in the conduct of heroes, devoted to the non-duality of substance, constantly serving the *samaya*, and auspiciously arisen from the *kula* and *kāla*. (36)

To one who is free from hypocrisy, who is self-guarded, and who delights in guarded conduct—from the seats (pīṭhas), whose forms are the seats themselves, [proceeds] he whose form is the seats, from whom the notes, smiles, and forms arise. (37)

Those who are eternally free from delusion, who act out of sight, who are filled with compassion, and who protect the observance of the rules of conduct—these are the ones [who guard the teachings]. || 38 ||
Through all their states and with great effort, the Mothers cause that supreme splendor which is gathered within them to blossom in the midst of the vital breath.
Impelled by them, the melāpas and other prosperities impel [the practitioners];
he exists as the manifest form of the heroes, abiding both externally and internally. (40)
In the Kaula teaching, for yogins such as Hṛdaya and the others, the secret is the attainment of the Knowable; this ground is unfathomable. 41.
The secret of liberation while living, the source of happiness for the Vīreśas, the essence of all essences, and the supreme destroyer of worldly existence has been told. (42)
The goal to be attained is generally a profound abyss, occurring by the hundreds and thousands;
therefore, with every effort, it must not be given to just anyone. (43)
This knowledge is for a single disciple; it must not be proclaimed by the great-souled ones. It stands outside all scriptures and is the heart within the Yoginī-kula.
